A Week of Global Cataclysms. And One Piece of News That Changes Everything

🌪 A destructive EF-4 tornado, as if straight out of a Hollywood movie, hit the streets of the Brazilian city of Rio Bonito do Iguaçu, becoming the most powerful tornado in Brazil’s recent history. Winds of up to 300 km/h reduced entire neighborhoods to rubble, leaving around 1,000 residents homeless and claiming 6 lives.

– A fire in Tongariro National Park destroyed 2,800 hectares in New Zealand;
– Arctic cold struck the USA
– a rare early snowstorm hit Canada 
– Japan experienced a series of 37 earthquakes in just over a day, including three powerful shocks with magnitudes above 6.0
– Two massive typhoons struck the Philippines: Kalmaegi claimed 232 lives, and Fung-Wong killed another 25 people
– Iran is enduring a historic drought
– In China “Hunzi Cloud Bridge” collapsed

The Delhi Government has organized a grand event at the Red Fort to mark the 350th Martyrdom Day of Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib. The celebration will take place from 23rd to 25th November. 

A grand event has been organized by the Delhi Government at the Red Fort to commemorate the 350th Martyrdom Day of Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that the celebration will continue for three days, from 23rd to 25th November.
The event includes Kirtan Darbar, Light & Sound Show, special exhibitions, and strict security arrangements have been put in place.                                     The Delhi Government, in collaboration with the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC), is hosting this programme.

On 19th November, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta visited the Red Fort to review the preparations for the upcoming mega event. During her visit, she was briefed about Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib’s life, and a lighting show was also showcased. She reiterated that the Delhi Government is organizing this grand programme at the Red Fort to honour Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib’s 350th Martyrdom Day.

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has appealed to the public to attend the grand event at the Red Fort on the occasion of the 350th Martyrdom Day of Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib.
She said the programme will feature a Kirtan Darbar, Light & Sound Show, and a special exhibition to spread awareness about the life and sacrifice of Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib.
In view of the event, Delhi Police has issued a traffic advisory and tightened security arrangements around the Red Fort.
The grand celebration will be held from 23rd to 25th November.
